summary: Iteration 13 (second run) — Google OAuth bridge + Hermes Admin MCP end-to-end (web + shared backend). Backend: 9/9 pytest cases pass (Google exchange rejects bogus session_id with 401; /auth/google/complete rejects accepted_legal=false with 422, missing token with 400, seeded valid token creates user with status=pending + account_type=client + legal_acceptance.method=google_oauth and consumes the pending row; GET /api/admin/mcp as admin returns {connected,endpoint ends /api/mcp, tools[14]}, as client returns 403, unauth returns 401; POST /api/admin/mcp/key generates dox_mcp_... key, JSON-RPC initialize/tools/list(14)/tools/call list_users|get_site_status|list_deals all return 200, rotation deactivates old key (old -> 401), new key works, missing/bad bearer -> 401, DELETE /api/admin/mcp/key revokes and the latest key is also 401 after revoke; client cannot POST /api/admin/mcp/key -> 403). Frontend: /auth?as=client and /auth?as=partner show [data-testid=google-signin-btn] on BOTH tab-login and tab-register; /auth?as=admin and /auth?as=underwriter never render it (count=0 on both tabs). Admin login (deptofx@proton.me / DoxAdmin!2026) -> /admin -> [data-testid=adm-tab-connections] 'Hermes MCP' tab renders mcp-endpoint='https://dox-prescreen.preview.emergentagent.com/api/mcp' (ends /api/mcp), mcp-status-badge='CONNECTED', mcp-generate-key, mcp-copy-endpoint, mcp-copy-config, mcp-tools-list with 14 tool cards; generate shows mcp-key-value once (length 62, starts 'dox_mcp_'), revoke button appears after generate. AuthCallback: /dashboard#session_id=<invalid> renders [data-testid=google-callback-error] 'Sign-in interrupted' — the full OAuth redirect is NOT automatable per /app/auth_testing.md and was intentionally not attempted. Note: admin login redirects to /workspace by default; the admin console is reachable at /admin and functions correctly.

minor.issue: GoogleExchangeIn.session_id has min_length=8; the auth_testing.md example uses 'bogus' (5 chars) which actually returns 422 (pydantic validation) instead of 401. Documentation vs. implementation inconsistency only — any session_id >=8 chars correctly returns 401 from Emergent. Low priority.

action_items: (Optional) Loosen or document min_length on GoogleExchangeIn.session_id so the sample curl in /app/auth_testing.md returns 401 as advertised, or update the doc to use a >=8 char fake session_id.

(Nice-to-have) After successful admin login, /admin is only reachable by explicit navigation; the login flow currently drops admins at /workspace. Consider role-based redirect to /admin for site admins.
(Defensive) Confirm /api/auth/login refuses empty password_hash so Google-created rows (password_hash='') can only be entered via Google — I did not verify this guard exists.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:690-729 google_exchange — Correct bridge: existing users get the EXISTING custom JWT cookie (set_auth_cookies) and never land in google_pending; new users get a 15-min pending token and must still clear admin approval. google_linked flag is additively set on the users row.

server.py:720-728 — google_pending row uses expires_at as a real BSON Date (datetime object); the TTL index db.google_pending.createIndex('expires_at', expireAfterSeconds=0) in server.py:393 relies on BSON Date, so this is correct.
server.py:736-737 — accepted_legal=false correctly returns 422 (semantic validation error) rather than 400 — matches the spec and the frontend's own legal gate.

server.py:755-787 google_complete — Writes an EMPTY password_hash ('') and auth_provider='google'. The downstream /api/auth/login endpoint must refuse empty hashes to prevent anyone with the email from logging in with ''. Recommend an explicit guard; not independently verified in this iteration.
server.py:2010-2018 _mcp_authenticate — Hashed-key compare via indexed dict lookup (hash+active). Updates last_used on every call; strips Bearer. Good.

server.py:2283-2301 — Key rotation uses update_many({},{active:false}) then insert — atomic enough for a single-active-key model. Rotation and revoke correctly invalidate ALL prior keys (verified by test: old key -> 401 after rotate and new key -> 401 after revoke).

server.py:2252-2265 /api/mcp — JSON-RPC batch supported (list body) with notifications filtered out. Error responses use custom 'detail' instead of standard JSON-RPC 'message'; MCP spec expects {code, message, optional data}. Functional but not strictly spec-compliant.
AuthPage.jsx:229,314 — GoogleButton is only rendered when audience is 'client' or 'partner', on BOTH tabs (login + register). Matches the requirement precisely.
AuthPage.jsx:349 GoogleButton — Hard dependency on window.location.origin + '/dashboard'. The REMINDER comment is appropriate; do NOT replace with REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL.

AdminPage.jsx:376 — endpoint computed from process.env.REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL; correctly surfaces the external URL in the admin UI (verified in screenshot: https://dox-prescreen.preview.emergentagent.com/api/mcp).

seed_data_creation: Test seeds a single google_pending row {token:testtok_iter13_abc, email:gtest_iter13@example.com} and cleans both google_pending and the resulting users row at test teardown. Also generates & revokes an MCP key during test_full_lifecycle (final state: NO active MCP key).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Regression file: /app/backend/tests/test_google_auth_and_mcp.py — run with `pytest backend/tests/test_google_auth_and_mcp.py`. It depends on mongosh being on PATH (/usr/bin/mongosh) and relies on an _mongo_eval helper that embeds DB_NAME into the MONGO_URI (because the default MONGO_URL has no db suffix). TestMcpKeyLifecycleAndRpc.test_full_lifecycle generates and then revokes an MCP key — it leaves the system with NO active MCP key. If a subsequent iteration needs an active key for UI testing, generate it via the admin UI or POST /api/admin/mcp/key. The real Emergent Google OAuth redirect to auth.emergentagent.com cannot be scripted — only the backend endpoints and AuthCallback error branch were exercised. To retest the happy-path /auth/google/complete, seed a fresh google_pending row via mongosh as shown in auth_testing.md.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Both features (Google OAuth bridge + Hermes Admin MCP) work end-to-end on web.
